newsitem.title: UK: Caution prevails in world bond markets - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Caution prevails in world bond markets - analysts.

text.p: Investors should remain cautious of global bond markets despite softer data in the U.S. but there are some short term opportunities in gilts and peripheral European markets, analysts said on Tuesday.
"One has to be cautious of global bond markets given the strength of the U.S. economy," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London.
Friday's U.S. April employment report showed payrolls below forecasts at 142,000, compared with 139,000 in March, but did little to dispel expectations that rates will rise.
"Although the tone is clearly positive, the Fed is nonetheless likely to tighten monetary policy at the May 20 (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting," Edmonds said.
But last week's U.S. economic data may at least postpone the date, if not the rise itself, economists said.

"It provides a breathing space, but there is enough strength in the U.S. economy to require another increase at some stage," said Brian Hilliard, chief economist, fixed income at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull in London.

"The key point in terms of the U.S. influence is that we have turned the corner on bond yields and even if there is some debate about when the second phase of the tightening is we are seeing generally rising yield trends."
Bronwyn Curtis, chief international economist at Nomura International in London, saw a rate rise in the second or third quarters.

"There is still a good chance that we will have a rate rise in the U.S. either in May or July just to take some of the exuberance out of the market," she said adding that bonds would rally, but not as much as might be expected.
"We are seeing growth in the economy and that means a squeeze on liquidity, so less money to be invested generally," she said.
The weakness in Treasuries was likely to affect the performance of global bond markets, analysts said.

"The cautiousness carries over to most bond markets," said Edmonds. "We are not likely to see European markets perform too well against the backdrop of weaker Treasuries and we have seen a fairly significant sell-off in the Japanese government bond market."

For investors in search of short-term value, Hilliard recommended looking at gilts. There, there was the likelihood of a reduction in the risk premium following the election last week of a Labour government for the first time in 18 years. He said three things would allow this premium to be reduced in the coming weeks.
The first was the 25 basis point rise in British interest rates announced earlier on Tuesday, to 6.25 percent.
"Secondly we have the Queen's speech next week which will lay down the legislative programme, and we have a mini budget within two months," Hilliard said.
"Those three things together will provide the confirmation the market needs that the Labour government will be true to its word, and that will dispel any lingering concerns."
Edmonds saw the chance of outperformance at the short end of European peripheral markets, particularly Italy.
"We've seen confirmation of good April inflation data and provided the government wins the confidence vote on the mini budget, we'll see a rate cut by the Bank of Italy fairly soon."
